skeleton:
Full English Breakfast Wrap

British · Easy · Makes 2 wraps

Jump to Recipe Method Troubleshooting Storage
The full English in soft flatbread: sausage, bacon, black pudding, mushrooms, tomato, and a soft scramble wrapped in a warm tortilla and griddled to seal. The wrap is the burrito's looser cousin — less engineered, quicker to fold, and friendlier to the wet fillings that the toastie bans: here the roasted tomatoes and mushrooms come along, and the wrap's generous circle absorbs what a pressed sandwich cannot. The technique is the warm-fold-seal sequence: a tortilla warmed until pliable, filled along its centre with a compact line, folded in the sides, rolled, and finished seam-down in a dry pan so the fold fuses shut. Sixty seconds of discipline per wrap, and the full English becomes portable in the tidy, holdable sense.

Quantities live in the recipe card.

The fillings (2 wraps)

The wraps

- **Cook the fillings first, cool them 5 minutes.** The burrito master's rule holds: hot fillings steam the tortilla limp and burst the roll. Components rested to warm-not-hot wrap clean. - **The tomato is deseeded** — seeds and gel are the wrap's wet enemy; the flesh dices clean and sweet. - One pan in sequence for the meats (the fat economy), a second for the eggs and mushrooms; the wraps warm while the eggs finish.

Full English Breakfast Wrap

Prep: 10 minutes · Cook: 15 minutes · Total: 25 minutes · Makes 2 wraps

Ingredients

The fillings (2 wraps)

  • 2 pork sausages (160 g), cooked and halved lengthways
  • 2 rashers (100 g) back bacon, cooked and halved
  • 100 g black pudding, seared and crumbled large
  • 4 large eggs (220 g), soft-scrambled with 10 g butter
  • 100 g chestnut mushrooms, browned
  • 1 tomato (120 g), deseeded and diced
  • 4 tsp (20 g) brown breakfast sauce
  • 20 g mature Cheddar, grated (optional)

The wraps

  • 2 large flour tortillas (about 60 g each, 25–30 cm)
  • 5 g butter, for the final griddle

Instructions

  1. **Cook the meats in one pan, 12 minutes.** Sausages whole first (10 minutes, turned), then the bacon for 4, then the black pudding for 3 — each in the accumulated fat. Rest, then halve the sausages lengthways and crumble the pudding large. Checkpoint — all three meats browned and cooked; the pan's fat used through, nothing poured away wastefully. Rested 5 minutes to warm-not-hot.
  2. **Eggs and mushrooms, 4 minutes.** Scramble the eggs soft-set (glossy, not wet) in the butter; brown the mushrooms in a second pan or after a wipe of the first. Dice the tomato. Checkpoint — eggs soft-dry — they finish in the wrap; mushrooms browned, not grey; tomato diced flesh only.
  3. **Warm, fill, fold.** Warm each tortilla 15 seconds in a dry pan until pliable. Down each centre: a stripe of brown sauce, then the eggs, meats, mushrooms, tomato, and cheese if using — in a compact line with 5 cm clear at every edge. Fold the two sides in, then roll tightly from the bottom, seam down. Checkpoint — a firm cylinder with the filling central and no bulging ends; the seam underneath, holding. Loose rolls burst; tight rolls with clearance never do.
  4. **Griddle to seal, 2 minutes.** Melt the butter in the wiped pan over medium heat and toast each wrap seam-down 1 minute, then turn for 30 seconds more — just enough to fuse and freckle, not to crisp the whole surface. Halve on the diagonal. Checkpoint — the seam holds when the half is lifted, the tortilla is freckled gold at the seal and still soft elsewhere, and the cut shows the full English in cross-section — egg, sausage, bacon, pudding, mushroom, tomato — every layer in its place.

Troubleshooting

SymptomCauseFix
Wrap burst at the rollOverfilled or cold-brittle tortillaCompact stripe, 5 cm clearance, the full 15-second warm
Soggy middleWet tomato or hot-assembled fillingsDeseeded flesh only; the 5-minute rest
Seam opened in the panSeam up, or no final griddleSeam down first; the butter griddle is the weld
Filling cold at the centreAssembled long after cookingAssemble within 5 minutes; the griddle re-warms the outer layer

Storage, Make-Ahead & Variations

- **Assembled wraps hold 24 hours refrigerated** (wrapped tight) and reheat seam-down in a covered pan, 4 minutes at low — the make-ahead version skips the final griddle until reheating. Fillings keep 3 days. - **Variation — the vegan wrap:** the vegan master's tofu scramble, shiitake bacon, and mushrooms in the same build; the tortilla never notices. - **Variation — the hash brown core:** a thin hash brown as the first layer — the potato slot filled and a crisp spine added. - **The format map:** the wrap carries what the toastie cannot (wet fillings), with less engineering than the burrito — the middle child of the handheld family, and the one for a picnic bench.
